text:
Nina (People Ops): Heads up 1 — new hire Lucas (Canadian) accepted offer as a software engineer. He plans to enter on a TN at the border/port of entry and start remote from Toronto for 2 weeks before flying to SF. Start date proposed: 2026-07-12.

Priya (Eng Manager): happy to be flexible. want him on projects ASAP but fine with remote first 2 weeks.

Lucas Tremblay: quick Qs: 1) do you need any docs from me before I cross? 2) can payroll start while I'm in Canada? 3) what does I-9 look like for a TN entry/start?

Nina (People Ops): quick answers: 1) yes we need the signed offer and LCA-equivalent TN support letter from us to present at POE; 2) US payroll typically starts once you're physically on US payroll and have US bank details; we can explore paying a short contractor for the remote period if needed; 3) I-9: Section 1 can be completed remotely; Section 2 must be completed in person after you are physically in the US (we can use an authorized agent in SF).

Marco (Immigration Counsel): notes (summary, not legal advice): For TN at POE, Lucas should carry: - Company support letter (we'll provide) - Offer letter - Passport + proof of Canadian citizenship - Resume + degree (carry copies) At the port of entry CBP decides to admit and will issue the admission. Employer should not give Lucas a visa stamp; TN is admission on entry. There's no USCIS petition. Important: TN admission is temporary and must be for a US position that fits NAFTA/USMCA categories. I-9: employer must complete Section 2 within 3 business days of the employee's first work day in the US. If Lucas is remote from Canada for his first days, complete Section 2 after he arrives in US. For payroll/tax: remote work from Canada can create Canadian payroll/tax obligations; consult tax/payroll.

Sana (Payroll): to add: Redwood's default is US payroll only. If Lucas stays resident in Canada and does work for >14 days we may need to run Canadian payroll or engage a local employer of record (EOR). Short stopgap contractor payments are an option. Need to confirm with Finance.

Eric (Tax): FYI from tax: if Lucas performs work physically in Canada while employed by a US company, Canadian tax withholding and CPP/EI may apply depending on days worked and residency. Also corporate permanent establishment risk if many employees are in Canada; one person is low risk but still flagged. Please confirm planned remote days and whether Lucas will maintain Canadian bank details.

Lucas Tremblay: thanks. Plan is: cross at Blaine/Peace Arch on 2026-07-11 evening, present docs, then work from SF office starting 2026-07-12. If CBP admits me same day, I'll be in US and can do Section 2. If not, I'll remote from Toronto for a few days. Do we have an SF agent for I-9? Also need clarity on benefits eligibility start date.

Nina (People Ops): SF authorized verifier: we use Workyer Verify (on-site at 525 Howard) or local Notary partners. We'll book a slot with the verifier on 2026-07-12 noon — hold that time. Benefits: benefits eligibility starts once you're on US payroll; we will share effective date scenarios.

Priya (Eng Manager): will keep 7/12 calendar clear for onboarding. fine with delayed I-9 completion if necessary.

Marco (Immigration Counsel): action items for docs: - Nina to provide a TN support letter template addressed to CBP (owner: Nina) - Lucas to carry original degree + transcripts and resume (owner: Lucas) - Marco to review support letter before finalizing (owner: Marco) Note: keep copies of the CBP admission stamp and Form I-94 record screenshot for our files.

Sana (Payroll): action items: - Sana to confirm whether Finance will approve contractor supplement for 7/12-7/16 if needed (owner: Sana/Finance) - Lucas to indicate bank/account preference (US vs CA) once admission confirmed (owner: Lucas)

Eric (Tax): action items: - Tax to run a quick residency/withholding check based on planned days in Canada vs US (owner: Eric)

onboard-bot: Reminder: please upload signed offer to `/onboarding/docs` and complete new-hire checklist 24 hours before start.

Lucas Tremblay: I'll scan my degree and passport and DM the files now. Also will screenshot I-94 after entry.

Nina (People Ops): sample wording for TN support letter we'll DM: "This letter confirms an offer of employment to Lucas Tremblay for the role of Software Engineer with Redwood Inference, full-time, starting 2026-07-12, duties, salary, and statement supporting TN classification under NAFTA/USMCA."

Priya (Eng Manager): thanks all. Lucas 1 excited to have you onboard.

Lucas Tremblay: thanks everyone. I'll report back with CBP outcome and post my I-94.

---
Quick checklist snippet to paste into `/onboarding/docs` (for Lucas):

- Signed offer letter (PDF)
- Employer TN support letter (provided by People Ops)
- Passport & Canadian proof (card/passport)
- Degree copy + resume
- DS-160 not required for TN (info only)
- Screenshot of I-94 / CBP admission
- Bank details for payroll
- If remote >5 working days, confirm contractor vs US payroll (Finance approval)

Nina (People Ops): will DM the TN letter and book I-9 verifier slot. Ping here once you have I-94. :party_parrot:
